parameters.name: ExternalIp
parameters.description:
The Elastic IP Address (EIP) that provides public network access.

The EIP must not be occupied by an SNAT rule of the same NAT gateway. You can check the IpLists.UsingStatus field returned by DescribeNatGateways to confirm that the EIP is in the Idle state.

parameters.name: ExternalPort
parameters.description:
The external port or port range for port forwarding.
- The port range must be within 1 to 65535.
- To forward traffic within a port range, separate the start and end ports with a forward slash (/), such as 10/20.
- If ExternalPort is set to a port range, InternalPort must also be set to a port range with the same number of ports. For example, if ExternalPort is set to 10/20, InternalPort must be set to 80/90.

parameters.name: ForwardEntryName
parameters.description: The name of the DNAT rule. The name must be 2 to 128 characters in length and cannot start with `http://` or `https://`.

parameters.name: HealthCheckPort
parameters.description: The health check port for DNAT. The port must be within the internal port range. Default value: empty.

parameters.name: InternalIp
parameters.description: The private IP address of the instance that communicates with the Internet through the DNAT entry.

parameters.name: InternalPort
parameters.description:
The internal port or port range for port forwarding.

- The port range must be within 1 to 65535.
- To forward traffic within a port range, separate the start and end ports with a forward slash (/), such as 10/20.

parameters.name: IpProtocol
parameters.description:
The protocol type. Valid values: 

- **TCP**: forwards TCP packets.   

- **UDP**: forwards UDP packets.   

- **Any** (default): forwards all packets.

parameters.name: NatGatewayId
parameters.description: The ID of the NAT gateway.

parameters.name: StandbyExternalIp
parameters.description: The standby EIP that provides public network access. The standby EIP must be bound to the NAT gateway. After the DNAT entry is created, the standby EIP takes effect.
